drills.title: METHANE Radio Drill
drills.description: You're on the radio. Pick the line that correctly belongs in each METHANE slot. Speed matters — dispatch is waiting.

items.why: M = the declaration (or 'standby'). Say the words.

items.prompt: Which line belongs in the FIRST 'E'?
options: Exit 14, northbound, under the rail bridge.
items.why: First E = Exact location. The last E = Emergency services.

options: Coach overturned into ditch after striking a lorry.
items.why: T = Type of incident — what happened.

options: Fuel leaking, live traffic in southbound lanes, powerlines down.
Approach from the north only; RV point at the truck stop, junction 13.
Approx 30 casualties: 5 red, 10 yellow, 15 green, 3 are children.
items.why: N = number, severity, and type of casualties — estimates are fine.

items.prompt: Which line belongs in the LAST 'E'?
options: On scene: 2 ALS, 1 engine, police. Request: 8 ambulances, 1 bus for greens, heavy rescue.
items.why: Last E = Emergency services present and required.

items.prompt: A dispatcher asks 'Confirm, is this a major incident?' The incident clearly exceeds your resources. You say:
items.why: Unambiguous plain language. Hedging delays resources; codes confuse mutual aid.

items.prompt: You don't yet know the exact casualty count. Best 'N' line?
options: 'Approximately 40, majority walking, at least 6 appear critical.'
items.why: An estimate with a severity split moves resources now. Refine later.

options: M-E-T-H-A-N-E: Major, Exact location, Type, Hazards, Access, Number, Emergency services
M-E-T-H-A-N-E: Medical, Evacuation, Triage, Hospital, Ambulance, Number, Exit
M-E-T-H-A-N-E: Major, Emergency services, Type, Hospital, Access, Number, Exact location
M-E-T-H-A-N-E: Mechanism, Exposure, Time, Hazards, Age, Name, ETA
items.why: Major – Exact location – Type – Hazards – Access – Number – Emergency services.
